stem.en: A carbon in the middle of a chain is bonded to two other carbons and two hydrogens. Kabir says "the two carbons must be opposite each other, 180 degrees, to make a chain". What does the sim show?

text.en: The two carbons are 109 degrees apart, like any two of carbon's four bonds, which is exactly why the chain zigzags.

feedback.en: Rotate the five-carbon chain. Every carbon-to-carbon angle reads 109. A straight chain would need bonds carbon does not make.

text.en: 120 degrees, because there are three things: two carbons and "the hydrogens".

feedback.en: The two hydrogens are two separate bonds. Four groups, tetrahedral, 109.
Right angles would put the four bonds on a flat cross, which the balloons showed cannot happen.

explanation.en: The middle carbon's four bonds are the same tetrahedron as methane's. Two of its corners happen to hold carbons. The zigzag angle is the tetrahedral angle.
